title: Oracle Database Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Oracle Database course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: Why use DUAL here?
options: The calculation needs no application table
It creates two copies of every row
questions.explanation: DUAL is a small built-in table used when a query needs no real table data. It is handy for trying a calculation.

questions.question: Which type is used for the text title?
questions.explanation: Oracle types describe the values a column or expression holds. NUMBER stores numbers, and VARCHAR2 stores variable-length text.

questions.question: How long does this named WITH result last?
questions.explanation: A WITH query gives a temporary name to a result used by that statement. UNION ALL keeps every supplied row.

questions.question: What makes the first row the shortest book?
options: The position of the file on disk
ORDER BY pages before the row limit
questions.explanation: FETCH FIRST limits rows after the chosen order. It can answer questions such as which sample book is shortest.

questions.question: Why use the DATE literal form?
options: To avoid an ambiguous text date format
To save the local timezone automatically
questions.explanation: A DATE literal names a calendar date in a fixed form. TO_CHAR can choose a clear display format for it.

questions.question: What does NVL use when the first value is NULL?
questions.explanation: NULL means a value is missing or unknown. NVL can supply another value when its first input is NULL.

questions.question: What is the join rule?
options: The author id values are equal
Both values have the same text length
questions.explanation: A join combines records whose key values match. It lets related facts stay in separate tables or query results.

questions.question: What does COUNT(*) count?
questions.explanation: GROUP BY makes one result per category. COUNT counts rows belonging to that category.

questions.question: What creates the numeric id automatically?
questions.explanation: An identity column lets Oracle create a numeric id. A primary key makes that id unique and required.

questions.question: Does rolling back a row insert guarantee sequence numbers are reused?
options: No, sequence values can leave gaps
questions.explanation: A sequence is a separate object that gives out numbers. NEXTVAL asks for its next value.

questions.question: Which procedure writes this demonstration output?
questions.explanation: PL/SQL adds variables and step-by-step instructions to Oracle SQL. A block can declare a value and use it in a statement.

questions.question: What does ROLLBACK TO before_extra cancel?
questions.explanation: A savepoint marks a point inside a transaction. ROLLBACK TO can undo later changes while keeping earlier work in that transaction.
